doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

chapter: The Rika band and funeral bands
title: Wilson and Landry's trumpet era, and the Tuxedo, Rika and Excelsior bands, c. 1931
summary: Martin and Russell recall the band's trumpeters and a funeral where three bands played, the Tuxedo, Rika and Excelsior. Peter led the Excelsior and Manuel went off to Celestine.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Yeah, I remember when Landry died, I went to... Landry died after Wilson. Yeah, I remember during Mardi Gras time.

Yeah, they had Hugh, Wilson, and Landry on trumpet. On trumpet, yeah. That's the time it was the Hugh Riker band. That's when they buried... Over the river they had... Henderson. Henderson. There had them three bands out there. That's there. Tuxedo, Ricker, and the Excelsior. Who was Henderson?
Was he a musician? No, he was Undertaker man.
Oh, Undertaker. Yeah. Oh, that's right. The band of music.
You always know that time. No, that was before my time.

No, that's in the...about 31. Yeah, I wasn't here. Oh, yeah. Well, I was going to ask about... Take Peter. Peter had leading the Excelsior band then. Peter, leading the Excelsior band. The more onwards, the more onwards, the more onwards, cause when Manuel had left and went up there to Celestine, and him and Celestine didn't make it and he come back to...the band that's called there. Excelsior? The more now, I'll share. The more now, I'll share. And Celestine. And that's the day they had DeFune, they had Manuel on trumpet, they had Peter on trumpet, and they had Love on trumpet. Oh yeah, they had a little bit of time. In the record they had U. On Trumpet, Landry, and Wilson. At Celestine, Emus Riley, no Mutt, Mutt, Mutt Kerry, in somebody else's own Trumpet. And that's the day they run Celestine. Couldn't find him. Oh yeah.
